intro: The Bears beat the Patriots 30-24 on Thursday night to reach 5-2, and the Chiefs, Vikings and 49ers head into Sunday as the league's unbeaten teams. Washington lost Terry McLaurin for the season, while Miami and the Chargers are still looking for a first win. 160 stories across all 32 teams.

top.label: Biggest Story
top.headline: Bears hold off Patriots 30-24 on Thursday night
top.dek: Caleb Williams threw for 308 yards and two touchdowns as Chicago moved to 5-2. Cairo Santos hit a 58-yard field goal with 1:34 left to make it a two-score game, and the Bears recovered the late onside kick.

top.label: Injury Watch
top.headline: Commanders WR Terry McLaurin out for the season
top.dek: McLaurin tore his patellar tendon late in the first quarter of Monday's 23-17 loss to San Francisco and needs surgery. He had 15 catches for 230 yards and a touchdown this season. Washington has lost three straight and is on its bye.

top.label: Player Spotlight
top.headline: Giants WR Malik Nabers is on a three-game 100-yard streak
top.dek: Nabers caught 12 of 15 targets for 165 yards against the Saints. His 168 career receptions through 25 games trail only Odell Beckham Jr. at 176. He shared the FedEx Air & Ground Player of the Week award.

top.label: Stat of the Day
top.headline: 0: offensive snaps the Dolphins have run while leading
top.dek: Miami has run 293 offensive snaps this season and none came with the Dolphins ahead. The 0-5 team has scored 70 points, 31st in the league, and allowed 132. Malik Willis has taken every one of those snaps.

top.label: What's Next
top.headline: Unbeaten Chiefs visit Seattle on Sunday Night Football
top.dek: Kansas City (5-0) plays the 3-3 Seahawks at Lumen Field on Sunday, 8:20 PM ET on NBC and Peacock. Former Seahawks running back Kenneth Walker III returns to face his old team. Watch the Chiefs' tackle depth against Seattle's pass rush.

teams.name: Buffalo Bills
teams.headline: Bills hit the bye at 5-1 with a leaky defense

stories.text: Bills carry defensive questions into the bye
stories.summary: Buffalo sits at 5-1 after a 33-30 win at Las Vegas that stayed in doubt until Khalil Shakir recovered an onside kick with 90 seconds left. The offense leads the league at 32.8 points per game, but the defense has allowed 29 or more points five times. The week off gives the coaches time to fix a unit that keeps handing back leads.

stories.text: Chubb and Kincaid back, Moore and Oliver still out
stories.summary: Outside linebacker Bradley Chubb and tight end Dalton Kincaid returned after being checked for rib injuries. Receiver DJ Moore (shoulder) and defensive tackle Ed Oliver (knee) both missed a second straight game. The bye gives all four extra recovery time before Baltimore visits on Nov. 1.

stories.text: Josh Allen leads the league in rushing touchdowns
stories.summary: Allen has 1,504 passing yards and 9 touchdown passes through six games, plus 240 rushing yards and a league-high 8 rushing touchdowns. Against the Raiders he went 23 of 33 for 255 yards and a score with no interceptions. NFL.com ranks him third in its Week 7 MVP tracker.

stories.text: 15: passing touchdowns allowed, the most through six games since at least 2005
stories.summary: Buffalo has given up 15 touchdown passes, second most in the NFL this season and the most through six games in at least two decades. Las Vegas converted 7 of 12 third downs and both fourth-down tries on Sunday. The Bills are 11-11 since 2019 when they allow 30 or more points.

stories.text: Bye in Week 7, then Ravens at home Nov. 1
stories.summary: Buffalo is off this Sunday. The Bills host the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 1 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS at Highmark Stadium. Watch whether the defense, rested and closer to healthy, can slow a quality offense.

teams.name: Miami Dolphins
teams.headline: Winless Dolphins still search for a first lead

stories.text: Winless Dolphins face the Jets at 0-5
stories.summary: Miami has lost five straight and has not won a game in Jeff Hafley's first season. Four of the next six games come against AFC East teams, starting Sunday at the Jets. A loss would make this the franchise's fifth 0-6 start and its first since 2019.

stories.text: Reese Taylor sits out, Willie Gay added with illness
stories.summary: Cornerback Reese Taylor (quad) did not practice Wednesday or Thursday, and linebacker Willie Gay missed Thursday with an illness. Edge Rob Beal Jr., receiver Caleb Douglas, tight end Will Kacmarek, safety Kyle Louis, long snapper Tucker Addington and running back Jaylen Wright were limited both days. Quarterback Malik Willis (thumb) practiced fully.

stories.text: Malik Willis runs for a franchise QB record
stories.summary: Willis has not topped 220 passing yards in a game and has two touchdown passes against four interceptions. His legs have carried the offense: he has 186 rushing yards, including 74 against Cincinnati, a franchise single-game record for a quarterback. Hafley has said Willis remains the starter.

stories.text: 0: offensive snaps run while leading this season
stories.summary: Miami has run 293 offensive snaps in 2026 and none came with the Dolphins ahead. The team has scored 70 points, 31st in the league, and allowed 132 through five games. Willis has taken every one of those snaps.

stories.text: At the Jets Sunday, 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Miami plays at MetLife Stadium against the Jets on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. The Dolphins have won 10 of the last 12 meetings, including a 34-10 win last Dec. 7. Watch whether Douglas returns and whether the run game, over 100 yards in four straight, can finally build a lead.

teams.name: New England Patriots
teams.headline: Patriots fall 30-24 in Chicago, miss too many tackles

stories.text: Bears beat Patriots 30-24 on Thursday night
stories.summary: New England never led at Soldier Field and fell to 4-3, ending a three-game winning streak. Cairo Santos kicked a career-long 58-yard field goal with 1:34 left to put Chicago up two scores. Mike Vrabel said of Drake Maye afterward, "He gave us a chance."

stories.text: Offensive line thins out again after Vera-Tucker lands on IR
stories.summary: Guard Alijah Vera-Tucker went on injured reserve with a hamstring injury. Offensive lineman Ben Brown and cornerbacks Carlton Davis, Karon Prunty and Channing Canada were ruled out for Chicago. Backups Walter Rouse and Matt Pryor started at guard, and right tackle Morgan Moses was hampered.

stories.text: Drake Maye throws for 321 yards in the loss
stories.summary: Maye completed 24 of 31 passes for 321 yards and two touchdowns, with one interception. He also led the team with 26 rushing yards and scored on a 7-yard run. Rhamondre Stevenson caught a 48-yard touchdown on the last play of the first half.

stories.text: 16: missed tackles against Chicago, the most since Super Bowl LX
stories.summary: PFF counted 16 missed tackles by New England, the most in a game since Super Bowl LX. The Bears gained 405 yards and Caleb Williams threw for 308 with no turnovers. The Patriots' turnover differential is minus 7, second worst in the NFL.

stories.text: At the Dolphins on Nov. 1, 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: New England has a long break before visiting winless Miami at Hard Rock Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 1 at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS. The Patriots are 1-3 on the road. Watch how the offensive line looks after another round of shuffling.

teams.name: New York Jets
teams.headline: Jets host winless Miami with Glenn under pressure

stories.text: Glenn is 0-7 against the AFC East ahead of Dolphins game
stories.summary: The Jets are 2-4 after a 26-19 loss at New England, and coach Aaron Glenn has lost all seven division games since taking over. New York has been outscored 119-49 in the closing minutes of the second and fourth quarters under Glenn, the worst margin in the NFL. Sunday's home game against winless Miami is a chance to change the trend.

stories.text: Breece Hall returns to practice on a limited basis
stories.summary: Running back Breece Hall (quad) did not practice Wednesday and was limited Thursday. Linebacker Kiko Mauigoa, running back Kene Nwangwu and edge Joseph Ossai did not practice either day, and lineman Max Mitchell was added with a concussion. Glenn said Hall remains the starter but Braelon Allen will get touches.

stories.text: Rookie edge David Bailey is piling up sacks
stories.summary: Bailey had three sacks in the Week 5 win over Cleveland. He is the only player since 1984 with 30 tackles, 5 sacks and a forced fumble through his first six career games. He gives the Jets a young pass rusher to build around.

stories.text: 119-49: the Jets' margin in closing minutes of halves under Glenn
stories.summary: Opponents have outscored New York 119-49 in the final stretch of the second and fourth quarters since Glenn arrived, the worst differential in the league per ESPN Research. The Jets have also allowed no points on opponents' opening drives in five straight games. The slow finishes keep costing them close games.

stories.text: Dolphins at MetLife Sunday, 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: The Jets host Miami on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. Rookies Kenyon Sadiq and Omar Cooper Jr. became the first rookie tandem to each post a 100-yard game in their first three career games, and Cooper had 6 catches for 103 yards against New England. Watch how the Jets handle Miami's run game.

teams.name: Baltimore Ravens
teams.headline: Lamar Jackson ramps up for Bengals

stories.text: Jackson returns to practice as Ravens fall from first
stories.summary: Lamar Jackson practiced on a limited basis Wednesday for the first time since he sprained his left ankle in the Week 4 loss to the Titans. Coach Jesse Minter calls him day-to-day. The Ravens dropped to 4-2 and out of first place in the AFC North after losing to Cleveland, and they went 3-1 with Jackson healthy.

stories.text: Jackson limited again, Robinson and Hawkins sit
stories.summary: Jackson was limited again Thursday, and a full practice Friday would likely clear him for his first start since Week 4. Edge Tavius Robinson (pectoral) did not practice for the second straight day. Safety Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) went from limited to out of practice, while Rashod Bateman, Ioane Vega and Ronnie Stanley moved to full.

stories.text: Derrick Henry carries the NFL's biggest rushing load
stories.summary: Henry leads the league with 130 carries and has the fourth-most rushing yards. Cleveland held him to 58 yards last Sunday, his season low. He needs 111 yards to pass Jerome Bettis for eighth on the career rushing list.

stories.text: 0: Points for Baltimore over its last nine drives
stories.summary: The Ravens went scoreless on their final nine possessions in the 13-10 loss at Cleveland. The Browns held them to a season-low 235 net yards and forced seven punts.

stories.text: Bengals visit Baltimore Sunday at 1 p.m. on CBS
stories.summary: The Ravens host Cincinnati in Week 7 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. Watch Jackson's ankle, the offensive line with Cam Jurgens back at center, and whether Henry gets going against a Bengals defense that allowed 155 rush yards per game over its last three.

teams.name: Cincinnati Bengals
teams.headline: Rested Bengals chase a division win

stories.text: Bengals come off the bye needing a win in Baltimore
stories.summary: Cincinnati is 3-2 after its Week 6 bye and has not yet won a division game this season. Joe Burrow said a win would put them at 4-2 and in control of their own path. The Ravens, Steelers and Browns all sit at 4-2.

stories.text: Dugger practices fully, Bengals enter healthy
stories.summary: Safety Kyle Dugger (quad) practiced in full Thursday, his first full session since he got hurt in Week 3. Defensive tackles Jonathan Allen and B.J. Hill had rest days. The team signed safety Russ Yeast from the practice squad to carry five safeties.

stories.text: Burrow has been efficient through five games
stories.summary: Burrow has completed 71.4 percent of his passes for 1,361 yards and 11 touchdowns through five games. Tight end Mike Gesicki has four touchdown catches in that span. Burrow has never been sacked by Trey Hendrickson, who now plays for Baltimore.

stories.text: 22: Straight field goals for Evan McPherson
stories.summary: McPherson holds the team record with 22 consecutive made field goals. Shayne Graham's single-game record of seven field goals came in Baltimore. Cincinnati will need him if the Ravens defense keeps drives short.

stories.text: At Baltimore Sunday, 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Cincinnati plays its second division game of the season at M&T Bank Stadium. Its run defense is the concern, having allowed 155 yards per game over the last three outings and 5.0 yards per carry through five games. Derrick Henry leads the league in carries.

teams.name: Cleveland Browns
teams.headline: Browns take first place in the North

stories.text: Browns win at the gun and lead the AFC North
stories.summary: Cleveland beat Baltimore 13-10 on Andre Szmyt's 37-yard field goal as time expired. The Browns trailed most of the way before Deshaun Watson led the winning drive. At 4-2 they hold first place on tiebreakers over the Ravens and Steelers.

stories.text: Quincy Williams added with a neck injury
stories.summary: Linebacker Quincy Williams was added to the report Thursday as a non-participant with a neck injury, and the extent is unknown. Safety Grant Delpit (concussion, shoulder), guard Elgton Jenkins and linebacker Carson Schwesinger moved from out of practice to limited. Defensive tackle Maliek Collins moved up to full.

stories.text: Schwesinger forces the fumble that turned the game
stories.summary: Linebacker Carson Schwesinger stripped Derrick Henry in the fourth quarter, and the recovery set up the game-tying touchdown. Audric Estime, signed off the Vikings practice squad Oct. 13, scored that 2-yard score. The defense held Baltimore to 235 net yards.

stories.text: 46: Net yards for the Browns in the first half
stories.summary: Cleveland managed 46 net yards and three first downs before halftime against Baltimore. The second half produced 191 net yards and 11 first downs. Watson went 3 of 9 for 24 yards in the first half and 16 of 26 for 164 in the second.

stories.text: At Tennessee Sunday, 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: The Browns visit the Titans at Nissan Stadium in Week 7. Cleveland has to start faster after its slow first half against Baltimore, and it will track the Williams neck injury. The Browns visit Pittsburgh in Week 8.

teams.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
teams.headline: Steelers fly to Paris riding an OT win

stories.text: Steelers rally past Tampa Bay in overtime
stories.summary: Pittsburgh beat the Buccaneers 26-19 in overtime on Oct. 18 and moved to 4-2. Rookie Germie Bernard caught the winning 6-yard touchdown from Aaron Rodgers, and Jalen Ramsey's sack on fourth down ended it. It was Mike McCarthy's first road win as Steelers coach.

stories.text: Highsmith limited with groin, two ruled out
stories.summary: Edge rusher Alex Highsmith was limited Thursday with a new groin injury. Receiver Ben Skowronek (calf) and cornerback Brandin Echols (hamstring) are out. T.J. Watt moved from out of practice to limited, and Ramsey (wrist) was limited after sitting Wednesday. Defensive tackle Sebastian Joseph-Day went to injured reserve.

stories.text: Rodgers ties Manning for third in career TD passes
stories.summary: Rodgers went 33 of 49 for 253 yards, two touchdowns and one interception against Tampa Bay. His winning touchdown pass was No. 539, tying Peyton Manning for third on the regular-season list. He led a 12-play, 70-yard drive in overtime.

stories.text: 23-3: Steelers' edge in the fourth quarter and OT
stories.summary: Pittsburgh outscored Tampa Bay 23-3 over the fourth quarter and overtime after trailing 16-10 late. Chris Boswell kicked three field goals in that stretch, and two interceptions kept the defense in control. Tampa gained just 32 yards in the fourth quarter.

stories.text: Saints in Paris Sunday, 9:30 a.m. ET on NFL Network
stories.summary: The 4-2 Steelers face the 2-4 Saints at Stade de France in the franchise's first game in Paris. Watch the health of Watt, Highsmith and Ramsey, plus a defense missing Cameron Heyward in practice.

teams.name: Houston Texans
teams.headline: Texans win in London on a last-play field goal

stories.text: Fairbairn's 49-yarder beats Jaguars 34-31 at Wembley
stories.summary: Ka'imi Fairbairn hit a 49-yard field goal as time expired to give Houston a 34-31 win over Jacksonville in London. Cam Little had tied the game at 31 with a 60-yarder just under two minutes earlier. The Texans stand at 2-4 with back-to-back wins. Marvin Harrison Jr. made his Texans debut after the trade from Arizona and caught 3 passes for 34 yards.

stories.text: Four Texans did not practice Wednesday or Thursday
stories.summary: Running back David Montgomery (groin), safety Jalen Pitre (shoulder), safety Reed Blankenship (concussion and hand) and tackle Blake Fisher (thumb) sat out both days. Tight end Dalton Schultz (quad) and linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair (knee) moved from no practice Wednesday to limited Thursday. Receiver Tank Dell (knee), tackle Trent Brown (wrist) and end Jadeveon Clowney (knee) practiced fully Thursday. The Thursday report lists no game designations yet.

stories.text: Stroud named AFC Offensive Player of the Week
stories.summary: C.J. Stroud went 24 of 34 for 312 yards and 3 touchdowns against Jacksonville, a 116.3 passer rating that led the league in Week 6. He drove Houston 36 yards in seven plays to set up the winning kick, the eighth game-winning drive of his career. It is his fourth AFC Offensive Player of the Week award.

stories.text: 1,714: Stroud's passing yards, second in the NFL
stories.summary: Stroud has 1,714 yards through six games, second in the league. He has thrown 9 touchdowns against 1 interception and carries a 100.9 passer rating while completing 64.0 percent of his throws.

stories.text: Giants visit Houston Sunday on FOX
stories.summary: The Texans host the New York Giants on Sunday, Oct. 25, at 1:00 p.m. ET on FOX. The Giants are 3-2-1 and have scored at least 27 points in each of their last three games while allowing 24 or more in each. Houston has to tighten up a defense that gave up 31 to Jacksonville.

teams.name: Indianapolis Colts
teams.headline: Colts fire GM Chris Ballard after Titans loss

stories.text: Colts relieve GM Chris Ballard of his duties
stories.summary: Owner and CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon removed general manager Chris Ballard on Monday, the day after a 26-20 home loss to the previously winless Titans dropped Indianapolis to 2-4. She said a change in leadership is necessary and that the team will run a thorough search for a replacement. The statement did not name an interim leader.

stories.text: Gardner, Warren and Gould still out Thursday
stories.summary: Cornerback Sauce Gardner (calf), tight end Tyler Warren (groin), receiver Anthony Gould (concussion) and punter Rigoberto Sanchez (foot) did not practice Thursday. Linebackers Bryce Boettcher and Austin Ajiake, guard Matt Goncalves and tight end Drew Ogletree returned to full participation. Cornerback Justin Walley (knee) was limited.

stories.text: Taylor piles up 151 yards but fumbles at the turn
stories.summary: Jonathan Taylor ran 21 times for 94 yards and a touchdown and caught 2 passes for 57 more against Tennessee. He also lost a fumble on the first play of the second half, forced by Jeffery Simmons, and the Titans scored off it. Indianapolis led 13-0 at halftime and scored 7 points after that.

stories.text: 399: Colts yards in a loss to a team with 186
stories.summary: Indianapolis outgained Tennessee 399-186 and still lost 26-20. The Colts piled up 232 yards to the Titans' 64 in the first half. A fumble, an interception in the red zone, a blocked punt and a 36-yard pass interference call swung the second half.

stories.text: Colts head to Minnesota to face the undefeated Vikings
stories.summary: Indianapolis plays at the Vikings on Sunday, Oct. 25, at 1:00 p.m. ET on CBS with Ian Eagle and Ross Tucker on the call. Minnesota has not lost this season. Daniel Jones sits atop the unofficial depth chart at quarterback, and the Colts must find a way to start the second half as well as they play the first.

teams.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
teams.headline: Jaguars hit the bye atop the AFC South at 4-2

stories.text: Jaguars take a last-play loss to Houston into the bye
stories.summary: Jacksonville lost 34-31 at Wembley when Ka'imi Fairbairn kicked a 49-yarder at the final whistle. The Jaguars still lead the AFC South by two games at 4-2. A holding penalty on Brenton Strange wiped out a Bhayshul Tuten touchdown run in the first half, and penalties extended two Texans touchdown drives in the third quarter.

stories.text: Harrison and Brown missed London, Murray battled concussion
stories.summary: Left tackle Anton Harrison missed the Houston game with a knee injury, and Walker Little started in his place. Cornerback Montaric Brown (hamstring) has missed two of the last three games. Safety Eric Murray missed Week 5 and part of Week 4 with a concussion. The bye gives all three time to heal.

stories.text: Travis Hunter makes plays on both sides in London
stories.summary: Travis Hunter caught 4 passes for 59 yards and a 7-yard touchdown that cut the deficit to 31-28 in the fourth quarter. On defense he made 3 tackles, broke up a pass and intercepted C.J. Stroud in the red zone, which set up Cam Little's tying 60-yard field goal.

stories.text: 273.8: passing yards allowed per game, 30th in the NFL
stories.summary: Jacksonville's pass defense has slipped to 30th in the league. The Jaguars have given up an average of 320 passing yards over the last three games. Stroud completed throws of 34, 42 and 50 yards that led to 17 Houston points. Safety Eric Murray said the secondary needs better communication and more time together.

stories.text: Bye in Week 7, then the Colts on Nov. 1
stories.summary: Jacksonville is off this Sunday. The Jaguars return in Week 8 on Nov. 1 against the Indianapolis Colts at EverBank Stadium, 1 p.m. on CBS. Watch whether a rested secondary can hold up before the Nov. 10 trade deadline.

teams.name: Tennessee Titans
teams.headline: Titans win first game, rally from 13-0 to beat Colts

stories.text: Titans erase a 13-0 deficit for their first win
stories.summary: Tennessee scored all 26 points in the second half to beat Indianapolis 26-20. It was Robert Saleh's first win as head coach, the team's first since Dec. 21, 2025, and it snapped a seven-game losing streak. A blocked punt returned for a touchdown was the Titans' first since 2011.

stories.text: Ridley's hip slips from limited to no practice
stories.summary: Receiver Calvin Ridley (hip) practiced on a limited basis Wednesday and sat out Thursday. Safeties Tony Adams (ankle) and Kevin Winston Jr. (quad) were limited both days. Running back Tony Pollard did not practice Thursday for rest, and linebacker Dorian Mausi (foot) returned to practice. No game designations had been posted.

stories.text: Rookie Carnell Tate scores his first NFL touchdown
stories.summary: The No. 4 overall pick caught 6 passes for 70 yards and tied the game with an 8-yard touchdown from Cam Ward against Indianapolis. Entering that game he led Tennessee with 29 catches and 344 yards. Tate said he plays faster as the reps pile up, and Saleh praised his yards after the catch.

stories.text: 14: points per game, last in the NFL
stories.summary: Tennessee averages 14 points and 235.3 yards a game, both at the bottom of the league. The Titans gained 186 yards against Indianapolis. Cam Ward threw for 102 yards, the lowest total of his career in a game he finished. The defense carried the day with 6 sacks and 3 takeaways.

stories.text: Browns visit Nissan Stadium Sunday
stories.summary: Tennessee hosts Cleveland on Sunday, Oct. 25, at noon CT (1:00 p.m. ET) on CBS. The Browns are 4-2 after a 13-10 win over Baltimore on a last-second field goal, and Deshaun Watson has 1,174 yards, 7 touchdowns and 4 interceptions. Watch Jeffery Simmons and Jermaine Johnson II against Watson, and whether Ward can move the offense. The Titans play at Cincinnati next, then take their bye.

teams.name: Denver Broncos
teams.headline: Defense carries Denver, Nix must lift offense

stories.text: Broncos defense has carried them, now Nix has to deliver
stories.summary: Denver sits at 4-2 because the defense keeps taking the ball away and pressuring quarterbacks. Bo Nix has 1,049 passing yards and six touchdowns, completing 60.3 percent of his throws, which is on pace for career lows. Coach Sean Payton said he must improve his own in-game planning and leadership to help the offense.

stories.text: Surtain limited again, Hufanga and Elliss sit out
stories.summary: Cornerback Pat Surtain II (ankle) was limited for a second straight day after missing Weeks 5 and 6. Receiver Jaylen Waddle (chest) was also limited. Safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle), outside linebacker Jonah Elliss (ankle) and running back Tyler Badie (thumb) did not practice Thursday. Running back Jonah Coleman, designated to return from injured reserve, practiced in full.

stories.text: Zach Allen leads a pass rush with 4.5 sacks
stories.summary: Defensive lineman Zach Allen has 4.5 sacks through six games. Denver sacked Seattle's Sam Darnold five times and hit him 17 more times in last week's 17-14 overtime win. Outside linebacker Jonathon Cooper is also back after missing six games on the Commissioner's Exempt list.

stories.text: 107: Nix's passing yards in the win over Seattle
stories.summary: Nix threw for only 107 yards in Denver's 17-14 overtime win over Seattle. He is in his third season with 1,049 yards and six touchdowns. The Broncos won anyway because the defense did the heavy work.

stories.text: Broncos at Cardinals, Sunday 4:05 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Denver visits a 2-4 Arizona team that has lost nine straight home games. The Broncos lead the all-time series 10-1-1. Arizona left tackle Paris Johnson Jr. is out for the season, and the Cardinals retire Larry Fitzgerald's No. 11 at halftime. Watch whether Nix and the offense move the ball against a team that cannot protect its quarterback.

teams.name: Kansas City Chiefs
teams.headline: Undefeated Chiefs hit Seattle with tackles hurt

stories.text: Unbeaten Chiefs face Seattle on Sunday night with thin tackle depth
stories.summary: Kansas City is 5-0 and heads to Lumen Field on Sunday night. Left tackle Josh Simmons and right tackle Jaylon Moore are both in doubt, which could put Kahlil Benson and Joshua Ezeudu on the edges against Mike McDonald's defense. Running back Kenneth Walker III also returns to face the Seahawks, the team he left in free agency.

stories.text: Simmons, Moore and Rice all missed Wednesday practice
stories.summary: Simmons (back) was listed as did not practice, and reporting describes the injury as a bulging disc. Moore is in the concussion protocol after leaving the Week 6 win over the Chargers at halftime. Receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring) has been out since Week 4. Linebacker Cooper McDonald returned to practice from injured reserve.

stories.text: Kelce plays through a rolled ankle
stories.summary: Travis Kelce rolled his right ankle in the first quarter against the Chargers and played most of the game anyway, finishing with four catches for 53 yards. He was limited in practice Wednesday. Through five games he has 20 catches on 27 targets for 299 yards and two touchdowns.

stories.text: 665: Kenneth Walker III's league-high rushing yards
stories.summary: Walker leads the league with 665 rushing yards. He now faces Seattle, which let him leave in free agency after the Seahawks won last season's Super Bowl. Seattle is 3-3 and Sam Darnold has been turning the ball over at a high rate.

stories.text: Chiefs at Seahawks, Sunday 8:20 PM ET on NBC
stories.summary: Kansas City plays Sunday Night Football at Lumen Field with Mike Tirico, Cris Collinsworth and Melissa Stark on the call. Watch the tackle spots, where inexperienced players may face Seattle's pass rush. Also watch Kelce's ankle and whether Rice returns.

teams.name: Las Vegas Raiders
teams.headline: Raiders try to end a three-game skid vs. Rams

stories.text: Raiders look to snap a three-game losing streak
stories.summary: Las Vegas is 3-3 after a 33-30 loss to Buffalo, its third straight defeat. The Bills outscored the Raiders 10-0 in the third quarter, and the offense went 2 for 5 in the red zone. Coach Klint Kubiak says the run game needs to improve, and quarterback Kirk Cousins wants fewer small mistakes.

stories.text: Bowers, Miller and Fatukasi go full on Thursday
stories.summary: Tight end Brock Bowers (hamstring/calf), tackle Kolton Miller (shoulder) and defensive tackle Folorunso Fatukasi (shoulder) were limited Wednesday and full Thursday. Defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway (concussion) moved from no practice to limited. Running back Mike Washington (foot/back) went from limited to no practice on Thursday, and linebacker Quay Walker (chest) was limited both days.

stories.text: Mike Washington pushes for more carries behind Jeanty
stories.summary: Rookie Mike Washington Jr. has 34 carries at 4.9 yards each, while Ashton Jeanty has 98 carries at 3.2. Against Buffalo, Washington ran nine times for 43 yards and Jeanty ran 10 times for 22. Asked if Washington earned more work, Kubiak said yes.

stories.text: 10: Las Vegas leads the NFL in takeaways
stories.summary: The Raiders have 10 takeaways, the most in the league. The defense missed its takeaway goals in two of its last three games, though. Las Vegas allows 27.0 points per game, 26th in the league.

stories.text: Rams at Raiders, Sunday 4:25 PM ET on FOX
stories.summary: The 2-4 Rams visit Allegiant Stadium with Matthew Stafford leading the league in pass attempts, completions and passing yards. Davante Adams is among their injured players. Bowers needs 18 catches to pass Trey McBride for the most by a tight end in his first three seasons.

teams.name: Los Angeles Chargers
teams.headline: Winless Chargers use bye to simplify offense

stories.text: Winless Chargers look to simplify offense during bye
stories.summary: The Chargers are 0-6, and Jim Harbaugh said that record gives nobody comfort. Mike McDaniel's offense ranks 30th in points per game at 15.0 and last in EPA per play, and the staff may cut down the playbook. The defense under rookie coordinator Chris O'Leary ranks 8th in success rate.

stories.text: Line injuries keep piling up during the bye
stories.summary: Center Tyler Biadasz is out for the season with an ACL tear, and tackle Rashawn Slater is on injured reserve. Joe Alt has missed the last two games, and Kayode Awosika has not played since Week 2. Safety Derwin James has missed three games with a hamstring injury.

stories.text: Rookie Akheem Mesidor gives the defense an edge
stories.summary: Mesidor, the No. 22 overall pick, has 2.5 sacks and a forced fumble. Fellow rookie Genesis Smith is tied for the team lead with two interceptions. Jake Slaughter has started every game at center.

stories.text: 99: pressured dropbacks for Justin Herbert, most in the NFL
stories.summary: Herbert has been pressured on 99 dropbacks, the most in the league. He has thrown eight interceptions, also a league high, and has thrown at least one in every game. Opponents have started drives in Chargers territory 19 times, also the most.

stories.text: Bye in Week 7, then Chargers at Rams on Nov. 1
stories.summary: Los Angeles is off this week and returns Sunday, Nov. 1 at SoFi Stadium against the Rams, 4:05 PM ET on FOX. Watch whether the simplified offense gives Herbert cleaner reads behind a patched line.

teams.name: Dallas Cowboys
teams.headline: Cowboys limp into Philly on a two-game slide

stories.text: Cowboys search for answers after a second straight loss
stories.summary: Dallas fell 23-13 to Green Bay on Sunday night and has lost two in a row. Dak Prescott went 34 of 54 for 258 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions. Brian Schottenheimer said the lack of a running game left the offense one-dimensional and blamed missed blocks and poor calls.

stories.text: Turpin doubtful, Winters doubtful, three more questionable
stories.summary: KaVontae Turpin and linebacker Dee Winters are listed as doubtful for Monday night. DeMarvion Overshown, Cobie Durant and Drew Shelton are questionable. Schottenheimer said Winters will be out for some time.

stories.text: CeeDee Lamb passes Tony Hill on the Cowboys receiving list
stories.summary: Lamb caught nine passes for 70 yards on 18 targets against Green Bay. His 7-yard catch on the final drive pushed him to 7,993 career yards, past Tony Hill for third in franchise history. He leads the NFL with 69 targets and has 48 catches for 577 yards this season.

stories.text: 4.3: Prescott's yards per attempt against Green Bay
stories.summary: Green Bay played zone on 76.8 percent of Prescott's dropbacks and held him to 4.3 yards per attempt, his fourth-lowest mark since 2018. The Packers kept safeties deep and forced short throws. Prescott wants his receivers to create more yards after the catch.

stories.text: Monday night at Philadelphia, 8:15 PM ET on ESPN
stories.summary: Dallas visits the 2-4 Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field on Monday, Oct. 26, with the game also on ABC and ESPN's streaming platforms per SI. The Cowboys defense ranks near the bottom of the league in EPA per play, and the offense has scored 29 points in its last two games. Watch whether Dallas finds a run game against a struggling Eagles offense.

teams.name: New York Giants
teams.headline: McCarthy gets the keys as Giants head to Houston

stories.text: J.J. McCarthy will start at QB over Jameis Winston
stories.summary: John Harbaugh announced Wednesday that McCarthy makes his first start as a Giant at Houston. He earned it with a fourth-quarter rally in the 34-27 loss to New Orleans, going 11 of 17 for 243 yards and a touchdown. Winston threw two interceptions in that game before the switch.

stories.text: Edmunds and Newsome sit out again, Thomas back to limited
stories.summary: Linebacker Tremaine Edmunds (shoulder) and cornerback Greg Newsome II (concussion) did not practice Wednesday or Thursday. Tackle Andrew Thomas (groin) and safety Jevon Holland (concussion) moved from no practice to limited. Final game designations had not been posted.

stories.text: Malik Nabers is on a three-game 100-yard streak
stories.summary: Nabers caught 12 of 15 targets for 165 yards against the Saints, tying his career high in catches. He has 168 career receptions through 25 games, second most in NFL history behind Odell Beckham Jr. at 176. He shared the FedEx Air & Ground Player of the Week award.

stories.text: 175: rushing yards the Giants gave up to New Orleans
stories.summary: The Saints ran 38 times for 175 yards against New York last week. In Week 5, Jayden Daniels ran for 103 yards and two touchdowns against the same defense. Houston ranks 25th in rushing yards, so the run defense faces a lighter test.

stories.text: Sunday at Houston, 1 PM ET, then a bye
stories.summary: The Giants visit the 2-4 Texans on Sunday, Oct. 25, at 1 p.m. ET, and then take their Week 8 bye. Houston has won two straight, and Will Anderson leads the NFL with 7.5 sacks. Watch how McCarthy handles that pass rush in his first start.

teams.name: Philadelphia Eagles
teams.headline: Eagles at 2-4 with McKee under center

stories.text: Eagles try to save the season without Jalen Hurts
stories.summary: Philadelphia has lost four straight, its first such streak since 2020, and scored just 58 points in those games. Hurts is on injured reserve with blood clots and is expected to miss the rest of the year. Tanner McKee is the starter as the Eagles host Dallas on Monday night.

stories.text: Saquon Barkley expected back at practice Thursday
stories.summary: Barkley has missed time with a hamstring injury since the Oct. 4 game against the Rams and has been considered week to week. League sources say he returns to practice Thursday. SI lists him as questionable for Monday, along with Carson Steele and several pass rushers.

stories.text: Tanner McKee takes over a stalled offense
stories.summary: McKee started the Eagles' 25-14 loss to Carolina, and the offense scored 14 points. His backfield is thin, with Will Shipley and Tank Bigsby on injured reserve and Steele hurt against the Panthers. Dallas Goedert needs one catch to move into third on the franchise reception list.

stories.text: 31st: the Eagles' rank in offensive EPA per play
stories.summary: Philadelphia ranks 31st in offensive EPA per play and 30th in success rate, and averages the fewest yards per play in the NFL. Its secondary ranks 25th in EPA per pass. Those numbers explain a team stuck at 2-4.

stories.text: Monday night vs. Dallas, 8:15 PM ET on ESPN
stories.summary: The Eagles host the 2-4 Cowboys at Lincoln Financial Field on Monday, Oct. 26. Dallas leads the all-time series 72-58 and won the last meeting 24-21 on Nov. 23, 2025. Watch whether Barkley plays and whether the offense finds any rhythm.

teams.name: Washington Commanders
teams.headline: Commanders lose McLaurin and head into the bye

stories.text: Terry McLaurin out for the season with a torn patellar tendon
stories.summary: McLaurin went down late in the first quarter of Monday's 23-17 loss to San Francisco, and Tuesday tests confirmed the tear. He needs surgery and had 15 catches for 230 yards and a touchdown this season. Washington has lost three straight and sits last in the NFC East.

stories.text: McLaurin done, Burks leaves with an unspecified injury
stories.summary: Besides McLaurin, receiver Treylon Burks left the San Francisco game with an injury the team has not detailed. Stefon Diggs and rookie Antonio Williams now lead a thin receiver group. Tight end Chig Okonkwo led the team with seven catches for 69 yards.

stories.text: Jayden Daniels threw for 300 yards in the loss to the 49ers
stories.summary: Daniels threw for 300 yards and two touchdowns and ran four times for 10 yards, but took four sacks. Over his last two games he has 499 passing yards and no turnovers. Dan Quinn says the offense will tweak its plays rather than overhaul them during the bye.

stories.text: 90: first-half yards for Washington in San Francisco
stories.summary: The Commanders managed 90 yards and two first downs in the first half Monday while the defense allowed 303 yards and 17 first downs. Quinn blamed pre-snap urgency and call selection on defense and wants more explosive plays on offense.

stories.text: Bye in Week 7, then Philadelphia on Nov. 1
stories.summary: Washington is off this weekend and returns to face the Eagles on Sunday, Nov. 1. Quinn says the staff will use the bye to tighten the offense around a smaller set of plays. Watch who steps up at receiver without McLaurin.

teams.name: Chicago Bears
teams.headline: Bears beat Pats 30-24 on Santos' 58-yarder

stories.text: Bears hold off Patriots 30-24 on Thursday night
stories.summary: Caleb Williams threw for 308 yards and two touchdowns as Chicago beat New England at Soldier Field to move to 5-2. Cairo Santos buried a 58-yard field goal with 1:34 left to make it a two-score game. Drake Maye answered with a late field goal, but the Bears recovered the onside kick.

stories.text: Kmet hurts right knee, Muhammad leaves with toe injury
stories.summary: Cornerback Malik Muhammad left in the third quarter with a toe injury. Tight end Cole Kmet hurt his right knee on a catch with 5:34 left. The Bears have not given a diagnosis for either player yet, so watch Friday's practice report.

stories.text: Luther Burden III goes for 130 yards in the first half
stories.summary: The second-year receiver caught four passes for 130 yards and a 24-yard touchdown against New England. Colston Loveland added a 12-yard touchdown catch. Burden gave Williams a deep target the Patriots could not handle.

stories.text: 58: Santos ties the franchise record with a career-long kick
stories.summary: Cairo Santos made a 58-yard field goal with 1:34 left. It was the longest of his career and the third-longest in Soldier Field history. The kick pushed a 27-24 game to a 30-24 lead that held.

stories.text: Bears head to Seattle for Monday Night Football
stories.summary: Chicago plays at Seattle on Monday, Nov. 2 on Monday Night Football. The Bears get extra rest after Thursday's game. Watch the Kmet and Muhammad injury updates before then.

teams.name: Detroit Lions
teams.headline: Lions off bye, host Packers with Branch set to return

stories.text: Rested Lions get Brian Branch back for Packers showdown
stories.summary: Detroit comes off its bye at 3-2 after a 45-21 win over Arizona in Week 5. The extra week let the Lions work safety Brian Branch back into the lineup. Green Bay arrives at 4-2 with three straight wins, so Sunday carries NFC North weight.

stories.text: Kerby Joseph out, Branch and Mays questionable
stories.summary: Safety Kerby Joseph is out Sunday. Safety Brian Branch, center Cade Mays and cornerback Rock Ya-Sin are all listed questionable. The Lions said they plan to play Branch and Mays barring a setback. Guard Ben Bartch, linebacker Devin White and receiver Tom Kennedy are on injured reserve.

stories.text: Jared Goff has 12 touchdowns and no interceptions
stories.summary: Goff carries a 111.3 passer rating, second in the league, while completing 67.0 percent of his passes. Jahmyr Gibbs averages 149.4 scrimmage yards per game and has scored in every game. Amon-Ra St. Brown has 37 catches and five touchdowns.

stories.text: 30th: Lions rank last in total and pass defense
stories.summary: Detroit's offense ranks second in scoring and fourth in total yards. The defense sits 30th in points allowed and last in both total and pass defense. Coordinator Kelvin Sheppard faces pressure to fix it. Aidan Hutchinson has four sacks and D.J. Wonnum has five.

stories.text: Packers visit Ford Field on Sunday at 4:25 ET
stories.summary: Detroit hosts Green Bay on Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET on Fox. The Lions are 2-0 at home this season and 20-7 at Ford Field since 2023. Watch whether the Detroit secondary holds up against Jordan Love.

teams.name: Green Bay Packers
teams.headline: Packers on a roll, Love's back a Detroit question

stories.text: Jordan Love says he will play at Detroit despite back issue
stories.summary: Love was limited in Wednesday practice with a back problem after taking hits in the win over Dallas. Coach Matt LaFleur said Love was pretty beat up. Love said he will play Sunday at Detroit. The Packers have won three straight to climb to 4-2.

stories.text: Parsons out again, three Packers questionable
stories.summary: Edge rusher Micah Parsons remains on PUP-R and is out Sunday as he recovers from a torn ACL. Cornerbacks Benjamin St-Juste and Brandon Cisse and guard Aaron Banks are questionable. Defensive tackle Jonathan Ford is on injured reserve. LaFleur has no concern about receivers Christian Watson or Matthew Golden.

stories.text: Love is on a career-best passing pace
stories.summary: Love averages a career-high 280.7 passing yards per game through six weeks, with 11 touchdowns and four interceptions. His completion percentage and passing success rate have slipped from last season. The run game has given him little help.

stories.text: 20-7: Detroit's record at Ford Field since 2023
stories.summary: The Lions are 20-7 at home since 2023 and 2-0 there this year. Green Bay's coordinators flagged Detroit's front seven as a major test for an offensive line that has struggled.

stories.text: Packers at Lions, Sunday 4:25 ET on Fox
stories.summary: Green Bay plays at Ford Field on Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET on Fox. Watch Love's back, whether running back Josh Jacobs returns, and how the line handles Aidan Hutchinson and D.J. Wonnum.

teams.name: Minnesota Vikings
teams.headline: Unbeaten Vikings return from bye to host Colts

stories.text: Vikings come off bye at 5-0 with an 11-game win streak
stories.summary: Minnesota returns from its Week 6 bye after a 23-13 win at New Orleans and hosts Indianapolis on Sunday. A win would make the Vikings 6-0, which they have not done since 2009. The team is chasing an NFL-leading win streak that stands at 11 games.

stories.text: Hockenson, Darrisaw and Addison back at practice
stories.summary: Tight end T.J. Hockenson practiced Wednesday after a head hit against the Saints and is expected to play. Left tackle Christian Darrisaw has been in concussion protocol since Week 4 and is encouraged about Sunday. Running back Jordan Mason is back from injured reserve, and wide receiver Jordan Addison is expected to play. Tight end Josh Oliver is out with a torn biceps.

stories.text: Aaron Jones carries the load: 370 yards on 85 carries
stories.summary: Jones has 85 carries for 370 yards over the past four weeks, including 113 yards at New Orleans. Jordan Mason is returning from a fractured thumb and could share the work.

stories.text: 12.8: points per game allowed by the Vikings defense
stories.summary: Minnesota has allowed 64 points through five games. The article compares the pace to the 1972 Dolphins. The defense also leads the league with a 47.8 percent quarterback pressure rate.

stories.text: Colts visit U.S. Bank Stadium Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Minnesota hosts Indianapolis on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET (noon CT) on CBS. The Colts are 2-4. Minnesota then faces a hard stretch: at Detroit, Buffalo at home, at Green Bay, and San Francisco in Mexico City.

teams.name: Atlanta Falcons
teams.headline: Falcons still hunting a first home win

stories.text: Falcons dig a 31-7 hole and fall to 2-4
stories.summary: Atlanta lost 31-23 to Chicago on Sunday and has not won at home this season. The offense gained three yards in the first quarter, and a rookie muffed punt set up an early Bears touchdown. The Falcons scored 16 fourth-quarter points to make it a one-score game, but the offense never got the ball back after a stalled drive with about five minutes left.

stories.text: Daniels, Deablo and Bowman sit out Wednesday's practice
stories.summary: Rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels is listed as a full participant Wednesday with a neck injury, three days after he left Sunday's game on a stretcher. He was alert and moving all four limbs that day. Linebacker Divine Deablo (hamstring) and cornerback Billy Bowman Jr. (forearm) did not practice, and A.J. Terrell (groin) and Brian Robinson (hamstring) were limited.

stories.text: Kyle Pitts finds the end zone twice against Chicago
stories.summary: Pitts caught five passes for 60 yards and two touchdowns, from 10 and 5 yards out, in the loss to the Bears. Jahan Dotson added a season-high 87 yards and a score on three catches. Michael Penix Jr. threw for 225 yards and three touchdowns, but took five sacks.

stories.text: 13: first downs for Atlanta against Chicago's 20
stories.summary: The Bears outgained the Falcons 368-257 and held a 20-13 edge in first downs. Atlanta ran 12 times for 63 yards and gave up five sacks. The Falcons are winless at home and have lost back-to-back games for the second time this year.

stories.text: Falcons host the 49ers on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET
stories.summary: Atlanta plays San Francisco at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on Sunday, Oct. 25, at 1 p.m. ET. Watch whether the Falcons can protect Penix and finally win at home. Their linebacker group is thin with Daniels and Deablo both hurt.

teams.name: Carolina Panthers
teams.headline: Panthers lead the South behind Bryce Young

stories.text: Panthers hold the division lead at 3-2
stories.summary: Carolina beat Philadelphia 25-14 on Sunday for its second straight win and sits atop the NFC South. Bryce Young threw for 281 yards and two touchdowns, both to Tommy Tremble. The Panthers now host a Tampa Bay team they have struggled against in recent years.

stories.text: Jaelan Phillips misses another practice with a hamstring
stories.summary: Outside linebackers Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) and Thomas Incoom (calf) did not practice Thursday. Chuba Hubbard, Taylor Moton, Devin Lloyd and Darren Waller all returned to full work after Wednesday rest days. Rookie tackle Monroe Freeling (knee), A.J. Dillon (ankle) and Bryce Young (knee) were full participants.

stories.text: Chuba Hubbard runs for 120 yards in Philadelphia
stories.summary: Hubbard carried for 120 yards and scored from 2 yards out in the fourth quarter against the Eagles. He has six touchdowns and 426 rushing yards on the season. His workload matters against a Tampa Bay run defense that ranks second in the league.

stories.text: 309.8: Bryce Young's passing yards per game, tops in the NFL
stories.summary: Young has 1,549 passing yards through five starts and a 98.5 passer rating. He is on pace for 37 touchdowns, and his career high is 23. Carolina's passing offense ranks first at 295.6 yards per game.

stories.text: Panthers host Tampa Bay on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Carolina plays the 1-5 Buccaneers at Bank of America Stadium on Sunday, Oct. 25. Tampa Bay has won 10 of the last 12 meetings. The Panthers' 27th-ranked run defense meets Bucky Irving, and they may face Baker Mayfield or rookie Jalon Daniels.

teams.name: New Orleans Saints
teams.headline: Saints take their skid to Paris

stories.text: Saints erase a 10-0 deficit and snap a three-game skid
stories.summary: New Orleans beat the Giants 34-27 at MetLife Stadium after trailing 10-0 late in the first half. The Saints then scored 34 straight points. Tyler Shough threw touchdown passes to Bryce Lance, Alvin Kamara and Chris Olave and also ran for a score.

stories.text: Carlson and Ruiz sit out Thursday's practice
stories.summary: Kicker Daniel Carlson (personal matter) and guard Cesar Ruiz (knee) did not practice Thursday, and defensive lineman Davon Godchaux sat for rest. Alvin Kamara (back), linebacker Kaden Elliss (calf) and edge rusher Anfernee Jennings (knee) were limited. Quarterback Tyler Shough (left hand) practiced in full.

stories.text: Alvin Kamara joins an exclusive 5,000-yard club
stories.summary: Kamara caught a 31-yard touchdown against the Giants and became the sixth player in NFL history with 5,000 career rushing yards and 5,000 career receiving yards. He joined Marshall Faulk, Lenny Moore, Marcus Allen, Christian McCaffrey and Tiki Barber. He is dealing with a back issue and was limited Thursday.

stories.text: 29.7: points the Saints allow per game, among the NFL's worst
stories.summary: The Saints rank tied for 30th in scoring defense at 29.7 points per game and 29th in total defense at 377.7 yards. They are 30th against the run at 138.0 yards per game. Their offense scores 25.3 points per game, 10th in the league.

stories.text: Saints face Pittsburgh in Paris on Sunday at 9:30 a.m. ET
stories.summary: New Orleans plays the 4-2 Steelers at Stade de France on Sunday, Oct. 25, on NFL Network. A win would give the Saints their first winning streak of the season. They have a Week 8 bye after the trip, then two home games.

teams.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
teams.headline: Mayfield nears return for a 1-5 Bucs team

stories.text: Bucs blow a 16-3 lead and lose in overtime
stories.summary: Tampa Bay fell 26-19 to Pittsburgh in Week 6 after Pittsburgh scored on four straight fourth-quarter drives. A 53-yard field goal sent the game to overtime, and Aaron Rodgers then led a 70-yard touchdown drive. The loss left the Bucs at 1-5, and Baker Mayfield is working to return from a thumb injury.

stories.text: Mayfield practices in full, Egbuka and Goedeke stay out
stories.summary: Quarterback Baker Mayfield (right thumb) was a full participant Wednesday and Thursday after missing three games. Receiver Emeka Egbuka (concussion, foot), tackle Luke Goedeke (calf) and linebacker Christian Rozeboom (finger) did not practice, and Rozeboom went on injured reserve. David Sills V came off injured reserve and is eligible to play.

stories.text: Rookie Josiah Trotter piles up 11 tackles against Pittsburgh
stories.summary: Trotter had 11 tackles and a pass deflection against the Steelers, bringing him to 48 tackles. The team says that is the most by a Buccaneer through five career games since at least 2000. Two more tackles would break Lavonte David's franchise mark of 49 through five games.

stories.text: 164.8: passing yards per game, 30th in the NFL
stories.summary: Tampa Bay's passing offense ranks 30th, and its scoring offense is 25th at 19.8 points per game. The Bucs went 6 of 19 on third down against Pittsburgh. Their defense is the bright spot, ranked fourth overall and second against the run.

stories.text: Bucs visit Carolina on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Tampa Bay plays at Bank of America Stadium on Sunday, Oct. 25, against the 3-2 Panthers. Tampa Bay has won 10 of the last 12 meetings. Watch whether Mayfield starts and whether the Bucs can slow Bryce Young, who leads the league in passing yards per game.

teams.name: Arizona Cardinals
teams.headline: Six Ryland field goals sink the Rams

stories.text: Cardinals beat the Rams 18-16 without a touchdown
stories.summary: Arizona went to SoFi Stadium and left with an 18-16 win in Week 6. Jacoby Brissett completed 24 of 35 passes for 218 yards with one interception and no touchdowns, and kicker Chad Ryland did the scoring. The defense also had its best day in a month after giving up 36 or more points in three straight games.

stories.text: Love, Baker and Nolen sit out Wednesday practice
stories.summary: Running back Jeremiyah Love (ankle), safety Budda Baker (groin and illness) and defensive lineman Walter Nolen III (ankle) did not practice Wednesday. Coach Mike LaFleur said Love is improving but will sit until he is at 100 percent, and he did not rule out Love, Nolen or safety Andrew Wingard for Sunday. Quarterback Carson Beck (back) and cornerback Max Melton (knee) were limited.

stories.text: Bam Knight runs for 80 yards as Love sits
stories.summary: Knight carried 15 times for 80 yards (5.3 per carry) against the Rams while Love missed the game with an ankle injury. Tyler Allgeier added 38 yards on 18 carries. If Love misses Week 7, Knight and Allgeier will share most of the work again.

stories.text: 6: Ryland field goals, and no touchdowns in the win
stories.summary: Ryland made six field goals, including a 43-yarder as time ran out, and they accounted for every Arizona point. The Cardinals reached the red zone five times and never scored a touchdown. It was their first win without a touchdown since 2017.

stories.text: Broncos visit State Farm Stadium Sunday at 4:05 ET
stories.summary: Arizona (2-4) hosts Denver (4-2) on Sunday, Oct. 25 at 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS. The Broncos rank near the bottom of the league in yards per play, while the Cardinals defense ranks 28th in yards per play allowed. Watch whether Arizona can turn red zone trips into touchdowns.

teams.name: Los Angeles Rams
teams.headline: Rams at 2-4 after a loss McVay called empty

stories.text: McVay says Rams must stop beating themselves
stories.summary: The Rams fell to 2-4 with an 18-16 home loss to Arizona as 12.5-point favorites. Sean McVay pointed to turnovers, penalties and a failed two-point try, and said he found nothing positive in the game. Matthew Stafford threw for 222 yards and two touchdowns, but a fourth-down turnover and a Tyler Higbee fumble stalled drives.

stories.text: Davante Adams out 6 to 10 weeks with hamstring
stories.summary: McVay said Adams ruptured his hamstring on a non-contact play late in Sunday's loss and will miss six to 10 weeks. The Rams have a Week 11 bye, which sets up a possible return shortly after it. Early reports described the injury only as a left leg problem, so the hamstring diagnosis comes from McVay's Monday update.

stories.text: Higbee may become a bigger part of the offense
stories.summary: Tyler Higbee caught all four of his targets for 22 yards against Arizona and fumbled on his first catch. The game ended a three-game stretch of five or more catches and 60 or more yards. With Davante Adams hurt, Higbee could move into the role of Stafford's second option behind Puka Nacua.

stories.text: 4.8: Stafford's air yards per attempt, a season low
stories.summary: Stafford averaged 4.8 air yards per throw in the loss, his lowest mark of the season. The offense settled for short passes while the special teams unit struggled, and kicker Blake Grupe is out for the year with a torn ACL. Los Angeles has now used three kickers this season.

stories.text: Rams visit Raiders Sunday at 4:25 ET on FOX
stories.summary: Los Angeles plays at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas on Sunday, Oct. 25 at 1:25 p.m. PT (4:25 p.m. ET) on FOX. The Raiders are 3-3 and coming off a 33-30 home loss to Buffalo, with Kirk Cousins starting again. Brandon McManus, signed Tuesday, is expected to handle kicking duties.

teams.name: San Francisco 49ers
teams.headline: 49ers hold off Washington to reach 6-0

stories.text: 49ers hold on to beat Commanders 23-17 and stay perfect
stories.summary: San Francisco improved to 6-0 on Monday night with a 23-17 win over Washington. The 49ers led 20-3 at the half after outgaining the Commanders 303 yards to 90, then had to hold on when Jayden Daniels threw two second-half touchdowns. Malik Mustapha broke up a fourth-down pass near the goal line with 1:54 left to seal it.

stories.text: Bosa, Samuel and Evans all hurt before Atlanta
stories.summary: Defensive end Nick Bosa (knee and calf) and receiver Deebo Samuel (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday, and Sports Illustrated lists both as out for Sunday. Receiver Mike Evans (ribs and Achilles) also sat out and is questionable. Linebacker Garret Wallow (hamstring) is out, and linebacker Luke Gifford (groin) is questionable.

stories.text: Purdy goes 21 of 29 for 264 yards on Monday night
stories.summary: Brock Purdy threw a touchdown to George Kittle and found Mike Evans for 24 yards on the third play of the game. With the night's work he passed the 1,500-attempt mark, which put his career passer rating of 105.6 ahead of Lamar Jackson's 102.7 for the best in NFL history. Christian McCaffrey added two rushing touchdowns.

stories.text: 14-2: Purdy's touchdown to interception ratio
stories.summary: Through six games, Purdy has 14 touchdown passes against two interceptions. He is completing 69.6 percent of his throws for 1,460 yards. San Francisco is the last undefeated team in the NFC.

stories.text: 49ers visit Falcons Sunday at 1 ET on FOX
stories.summary: San Francisco goes for 7-0 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on Sunday, Oct. 25 at 1 p.m. ET on FOX. Atlanta is 2-4. Watch how the 49ers cover for Bosa and Samuel, and whether Evans plays.

teams.name: Seattle Seahawks
teams.headline: Seahawks seek a fix after overtime loss

stories.text: Seahawks lose to Broncos 17-14 in overtime
stories.summary: Denver beat Seattle 17-14 on Thursday, Oct. 15, when Wil Lutz kicked a 53-yard field goal in overtime. Seattle (3-3) cut the lead to 14-11 late, but Sam Darnold threw interceptions at the end of regulation and in overtime. Rashid Shaheed also lost a fumble and muffed the opening overtime kickoff.

stories.text: Charbonnet practices fully, three linebackers sit
stories.summary: Running back Zach Charbonnet practiced fully for the first time since February ACL surgery, and coach Mike Macdonald said he could play in some capacity Sunday. Linebackers Drake Thomas (ankle), Chazz Surratt (calf) and Connor O'Toole (hamstring) did not practice Thursday. Quarterback Drew Lock (right elbow) was limited.

stories.text: Smith-Njigba catches 12 for 134 yards in the loss
stories.summary: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 12 of 16 targets for 134 yards against Denver. He converted a fourth-and-4 to keep a touchdown drive alive and made a 32-yard catch that set up Seattle in Denver territory late in regulation. He leads the league in receiving yards and receiving touchdowns, per NBC.

stories.text: 5: sacks Darnold took against Denver
stories.summary: Darnold went 27 of 51 for 278 yards with no touchdowns, two interceptions and five sacks in the overtime loss. Seattle's rushing attack ranks last in the league in rush EPA. The offense leans heavily on Smith-Njigba.

stories.text: Unbeaten Chiefs visit Seattle on Sunday Night Football
stories.summary: Seattle hosts Kansas City (5-0) at Lumen Field on Sunday, Oct. 25 at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC and Peacock. Former Seahawks running back Kenneth Walker III returns to face his old team. Seattle is 3-3 and will test its defense against one of three unbeaten teams.
